requirement.summary: POS - Request to add more information in the audit log description
requirement.description:
Background:

Currently, the audit log for Change Table can only show the new table information, there is no from table information on the description.  Suggest to add from table information in the Audit Log.

Enhancement Request:

Add the from table information in the Audit Log description.

Current description sample: Change table number to (102)

Sample 2: Change table number to (107C)

Request new description: Change table number from (101) to (102)

Sample 2: Change table number from (107A) to (107C)

The scope should include the change table from workstation / POS API

20260810

Add discount code when apply discount

Add user no. when apply print check
requirement.release_notes:
Enhancements: [Jira-62878] Add from table information in the audit log description (Simon Li)
Descriptions:
It is available for the normal workstation and the API Portal
System supports showing the full change table information in the audit log description for audit log type "Change table for old check", after performing function “Change Table”, “Void Paid Check”, “Force Void Paid Check”, as well as API portal endpoint “Change Table”, when the table is changed successfully
The audit log description now is updated to "Change table number from (Original table number with table extension) to (Target table number with table extension)"
Workflow of "Change Table" in the normal workstation
1. Open an old check
2. Click function "Change Table"
3. System prompts the change table screen
4. Enter the target table and table extension
5. Click button "OK"
6. System follows the existing workflow to change the table
7. If the table change is successful, go to step 9
8. If the table change fails, system follows the existing workflow to prompt the error message and abort the action
9. System writes an audit log with the following description: Change table number from (Original table number with table extension) to (Target table number with table extension)
Workflow of "Change Table" in the API Portal
1. System receives the API request for an old check
2. System follows the existing workflow to change the table
3. If the table change is successful, go to step 5
4. If the table change fails, system follows the existing workflow to return an error message and abort the action
5. System writes an audit log with the following description: Change table number from (Original table number with table extension) to (Target table number with table extension)
Workflow of "Void Paid Check" / "Force Void Paid Check" in the normal workstation
1. Click button "Admin"
2. Select tab "Check Operation"
3. Click function "Check Listing"
4. Select the target paid check
5. System prompts the receipt preview of the selected check
6. Click function "Void Paid Check" or "Force Void Paid Check"
7. System prompts the void reason screen
8. Select the target void reason
9. System releases the payment
10. If the payment is released successfully, go to step 12
11. If the payment release fails, system follows the existing workflow to prompt the error message and abort the action
12. System voids the check
13. If the void is successful, system follows the existing workflow to continue the operation and the workflow ends here
14. If the void fails, go to step 15
15. System follows existing workflow for update table information for check
16. If table is successfully changed, system writes an audit log with the following description: Change table number from (Original table number with table extension) to (Target table number with table extension)
Setup:
None

requirement.summary: POS Function - Duty Meal / On Credit Limits - Allow Decimal Values for Payment Method Limit Balance
requirement.description:
User Story

As an administrator, I want to enter decimal values for Duty Meal and On Credit limit settings so that I can configure precise balance limits that match real-world fractional currency amounts.

Current Behavior

The POS configuration for Duty Meal and On Credit limit settings only accepts positive integer values. Administrators cannot enter or save amounts with decimal places (e.g., 10.50, 25.75). The existing 'Duty Meal/On Credit User Group Shop Limit Setting' and 'Duty Meal/On Credit User Shop Limit Setting' CBL settings already support unrestricted decimal places and serve as the reference pattern.

Expected Behavior

All eight Duty Meal and On Credit limit settings should accept positive decimal values with no cap on the number of decimal places, matching the existing 'Duty Meal/On Credit User Group Shop Limit Setting' and 'Duty Meal/On Credit User Shop Limit Setting' CBL settings. Values should be saved exactly as entered. The affected settings are: Duty Meal User Group Payment Method Limit, Duty Meal Shop Limit, Duty Meal Outlet Limit, Duty Meal Check Limit, On Credit User Group Payment Method Limit, On Credit Shop Limit, On Credit Outlet Limit, and On Credit Check Limit.

Acceptance Criteria

Enter decimal value for Duty Meal limit settings

- Given a Duty Meal limit setting (User Group Payment Method, Shop, Outlet, or Check) is open

- When the administrator enters a positive decimal value such as 10.50

- Then the value is accepted and saved exactly as entered

- And the value is displayed and processed correctly throughout the POS application

Enter decimal value for On Credit limit settings

- Given an On Credit limit setting (User Group Payment Method, Shop, Outlet, or Check) is open

- When the administrator enters a positive decimal value such as 25.75

- Then the value is accepted and saved exactly as entered

- And the value is displayed and processed correctly throughout the POS application

Unrestricted decimal places

- Given a Duty Meal or On Credit limit setting is open

- When the administrator enters a value with multiple decimal places such as 10.999

- Then the value is saved exactly as entered with no cap on decimal places

- And the behavior matches the existing 'Duty Meal/On Credit User Group Shop Limit Setting' and 'Duty Meal/On Credit User Shop Limit Setting' settings

Existing integer values remain supported

- Given a Duty Meal or On Credit limit setting is open

- When the administrator enters a positive integer value such as 10

- Then the value is accepted and saved without changes

- But if the administrator enters a negative value or non-numeric text, the value is rejected and not saved

- And if the administrator enters zero, the value is rejected and not saved

Supporting Evidence

Jira Case Reference: HERO-62752

Zoho Desk Number: 255139001004309614

Requested Timeline

Aligned with Priority: Medium

Preferred Quarter: Not specified

Notes: No fixed deadline provided by requester.

Alternatives Considered

Capping decimal places at standard currency precision (2 decimal places) was considered, but the requester confirmed the number of decimal places should be unrestricted, matching the existing 'Duty Meal/On Credit User Group Shop Limit Setting' and 'Duty Meal/On Credit User Shop Limit Setting' CBL settings.

Original Description (preserved by INF Prod. Studio)

Enhancement Details

Similar to CBL 'Duty Meal/On Credit User Group Shop Limit Setting' and 'Duty Meal/On Credit User Shop Limit Setting'

All other Duty Meal and On Credit limit CBL setting should support no limit decimal place setting.

Existing example as mentioned above:

This enhancement is request to support allowing to set decimal places for below CBL with no limit on the number of decimal places as above sample:

- Duty Meal User Group Payment Method Limit

- Duty Meal Shop Limit

- Duty Meal Outlet Limit

- Duty Meal Check Limit

- On Credit User Group Payment Method Limit

- On Credit Shop Limit

- On Credit Outlet Limit

- On Credit Check Limit

_______________________________________________________________________________________________{}

Requested Enhancement

Jira Case Reference: https://jira.shijidev.com/browse/HERO-62752

Modify the POS configuration to allow decimal values for the following payment method limits:

- Duty Meal Payment Method Limit Balance

- On Credit User Group Payment Method Limit Balance

- User Module Information (Duty Meal and On Credit)

- Config By Location:

- Duty Meal Shop Limit

- Duty Meal Outlet Limit

- Duty Meal Check Limit

- Duty Meal User Group Shop Limit Setting

- Duty Meal User Shop Limit Setting

- Duty Meal User Group Payment Method Limit

- On Credit Shop Limit

- On Credit Outlet Limit

- On Credit Check Limit

- On Credit User Group Shop Limit Setting

- On Credit User Shop Limit Setting

- On Credit User Group Payment Method Limit

Zoho Desk Number: https://support-intl.shijigroup.com/agent/shijigroupintl/infrasys-support/tickets/details/255139001004309614

Current Behavior

- Field accepts positive integers only.

- Decimal values (e.g., 10.50, 25.75) cannot be entered or saved.

Expected Behavior

- Field should accept positive decimal values.

- Support standard currency precision (e.g., up to 2 decimal places).

- Existing integer values should continue to be supported without changes.

Business Justification Allowing decimal values provides greater flexibility and accuracy when configuring Duty Meal and On Credit payment limits. This aligns the configuration with real-world currency requirements and prevents administrators from being restricted to whole-number amounts only.

Example

| Scenario
| Current Result
| Expected Result

| Limit = 10
| Accepted
| Accepted

| Limit = 10.50
| Rejected
| Accepted

| Limit = 25.75
| Rejected
| Accepted

Acceptance Criteria

- Users can enter positive decimal values for Duty Meal Payment Method Limit Balance.

- Users can enter positive decimal values for On Credit User Group Payment Method Limit Balance.

- System validates and saves decimal values successfully.

- Existing integer values remain supported.

- Decimal values are correctly displayed and processed throughout the POS application.

- No impact on existing configurations or payment workflows.

requirement.summary: Report - TMS024 Waiting List Extraction - Add Syndicate Owner Indicator field
requirement.description:
User Story

As a report user, I want the Syndicate Owner Indicator field displayed in the TMS024 Waiting List Extraction report so that I can identify whether a reservation has a syndicate owner assigned without opening the reservation record.

Current Behavior

The TMS024 Waiting List Extraction report does not display the Syndicate Owner Indicator field. The field is stored in the TMS reservation record (DB field: hkjc_resv_members: rmem_syndicate_owner_indicator) but is not surfaced in this report.

Expected Behavior

The TMS024 Waiting List Extraction report displays a new "Syndicate Owner Indicator" field positioned to the LEFT of the existing "Syndicate Owner" field. The field appears in all output formats: on-screen, printed, and exported. It is purely a display column and does not affect existing sorting or grouping behaviour. Display values: Y = Yes, N = No, blank = reservation uses an offline profile with no Syndicate Owner Indicator.

Acceptance Criteria

Display Syndicate Owner Indicator field

- Given the TMS024 Waiting List Extraction report is generated

- When the report renders

- Then a new Syndicate Owner Indicator column appears immediately to the LEFT of the Syndicate Owner column

- And the column is present in on-screen, printed, and exported (e.g. PDF, Excel) output formats

Display indicator values

- Given a reservation has a syndicate owner indicator value stored in the database

- When the report renders that reservation row

- Then the Syndicate Owner Indicator column displays Y when the value is Y

- But the column displays N when the value is N

- And the column displays blank when the value is empty (reservation uses an offline profile with no Syndicate Owner Indicator)

Preserve sorting and grouping

- Given the TMS024 report has existing sorting or grouping by syndicate owner

- When the Syndicate Owner Indicator column is added

- Then the existing sorting and grouping behaviour remains unchanged

- And the new column does not introduce any additional sorting or grouping

Supporting Evidence

DB field: hkjc_resv_members: rmem_syndicate_owner_indicator (confirmed with TMS team). Data source is confirmed and available for all 10 reports. Scope of this ticket is limited to TMS024 only; the other 9 reports are tracked in separate tickets.

Preferred Quarter: not specified

Notes: no fixed deadline provided by requester

requirement.summary: Report - TMS022 Master Pre-Race Booking List - Add Syndicate Owner Indicator field
requirement.description:
User Story

As a TMS report user, I want the Syndicate Owner Indicator field displayed in the TMS022 Master Pre-Race Booking List report so that I can see the indicator value directly alongside the Syndicate Owner without cross-referencing the reservation record or other systems.

Current Behavior

The TMS022 Master Pre-Race Booking List report does not display the Syndicate Owner Indicator field. The value is stored in the reservation record (DB field: hkjc_resv_members: rmem_syndicate_owner_indicator) but is not surfaced in this report, so users cannot see the indicator on screen, in printed output, or in exported data files.

Expected Behavior

The TMS022 Master Pre-Race Booking List report displays a new "Syndicate Owner Indicator" column on the LEFT of the existing "Syndicate Owner" column. The column appears in both the on-screen preview and the printed/exported output, and is included in any exported data files (Excel/CSV). The column is always populated for every reservation, with values rendered as Y, N, or blank.

Acceptance Criteria

Add Syndicate Owner Indicator column

- Given a user opens the TMS022 Master Pre-Race Booking List report

- When the report is generated

- Then a new Syndicate Owner Indicator column appears on the LEFT of the Syndicate Owner column

- And the column is populated for every reservation row

Render indicator values

- Given a reservation has a Syndicate Owner Indicator value in the database

- When the report is generated

- Then a value of Y is displayed as Y

- And a value of N is displayed as N

- And an empty value (reservation using an offline profile with no Syndicate Owner Indicator) is displayed as blank

- But if the database contains any value other than Y, N, or empty, the report renders it without error and does not crash

Show in preview and printed output

- Given a user views the TMS022 report

- When the report is previewed on screen or printed/exported

- Then the Syndicate Owner Indicator column is shown in both the on-screen preview and the printed/exported output

- And the column position (left of Syndicate Owner) is consistent across preview and printed output

Include in exported data files

- Given a user exports the TMS022 report to Excel or CSV

- When the export file is generated

- Then the Syndicate Owner Indicator field is included in the exported data file

- And the exported values match the on-screen values (Y, N, or blank)

- But if the export contains no reservations, the column header is still present in the exported file

Supporting Evidence

The Syndicate Owner Indicator field was added to the TMS reservation record in HERO-64070 and HERO-67705.

requirement.summary: POS Export - SUN Cover Export v2 Support TXT Export Format
requirement.description:
Background / Current Situation

The SUN cover v2 (sun_cover_account_v2_export) currently supports export in NDF format only.

For Swire Hotels, the exported file is required in TXT format. At present, the NDF file has to be manually converted to TXT before it can be used.

Requirement

Enhance the SUN POS Export Program to support selection of the export file format.

In the Export File Setup section, add a new Export File Format option with the following selections:

- NDF – Default

- TXT

The default value should remain NDF to maintain the current system behavior and compatibility with existing customers.

When TXT is selected, the export program should generate the export file in TXT format accordingly.

Acceptance Criteria

- A new Export File Format selection is available in the SUN POS Export Program configuration.

- The available options are NDF and TXT.

- NDF is selected by default.

- When NDF is selected, the existing export behavior remains unchanged.

- When TXT is selected, the exported file is generated in TXT format.

- No other existing export logic or configuration is affected.

requirement.summary: Report - MENU003 - Add Optional Department/Category Change Columns
requirement.description:
User Story

As a hotel maintenance reviewer, I want the MENU003 Item Maintenance Report to optionally display Department/Category change details so that I can review inventory cost-impacting configuration changes directly within the report without cross-referencing the Audit Log.

Current Behavior

MENU003 Item Maintenance Report does not display Department/Category change information. Users must navigate to the Audit Log separately to identify and review these changes. There is no way to correlate item maintenance records with their Department/Category change history within a single report view.

Expected Behavior

MENU003 Item Maintenance Report includes a new report parameter "Include changes for Department/Category" with a default value of Off/No. When enabled, the report displays one row per Department/Category change event with two additional columns: "Department/Category (From)" and "Department/Category (To)". Changes are captured from all sources: bulk import, API, HQ back-office, and POS Item Maintenance. Only items that had at least one Department/Category change within the report's date range are shown. The new columns appear consistently across all output formats: on-screen report view, print, and export (CSV/Excel/PDF).

Acceptance Criteria

New report parameter is available with correct default

- Given the user accesses the MENU003 report parameters screen

- When the user views the available parameter options

- Then a new parameter labeled 'Include changes for Department/Category' is present

- And the parameter default value is No

- And the parameter is accessible to all users who have permission to run MENU003

Parameter disabled preserves existing report behavior

- Given the 'Include changes for Department/Category' parameter is set to No

- When the user generates the MENU003 report

- Then the report layout, columns, and output are identical to the current MENU003 behavior

- And no 'Department/Category (From)' or 'Department/Category (To)' columns appear in any output format

- And all items within the report date range are displayed regardless of whether they had Department/Category changes

Parameter enabled displays change columns in all output formats

- Given the 'Include changes for Department/Category' parameter is set to Yes

- When the user generates the MENU003 report

- Then the report includes 'Department/Category (From)' and 'Department/Category (To)' columns

- And the columns appear in on-screen report view

- And the columns appear in printed output

- And the columns appear in all export formats: CSV, Excel, and PDF

- But if no items in the report date range had a Department/Category change, the report displays an empty result set with the new column headers visible

One row per change event with correct From/To values

- Given the 'Include changes for Department/Category' parameter is enabled and the report date range includes an item that had its Department/Category changed three times

- When the user generates the MENU003 report

- Then the item appears as three separate rows, one per change event

- And each row shows the Department/Category value before the change in the 'From' column and the value after the change in the 'To' column

- And the From/To values match the corresponding change records in the Audit Log

- And each row includes the timestamp of the change event

- But if a change event occurred outside the report date range, that event is excluded from the results

Changes from all sources are captured

- Given the 'Include changes for Department/Category' parameter is enabled

- When the report runs for a date range containing Department/Category changes made via different sources

- Then changes made through bulk import are included

- And changes made through API calls are included

- And changes made through HQ back-office are included

- And changes made through POS Item Maintenance screen are included

- And the source of each change is identifiable in the report output

Supporting Evidence

Existing Audit Log already captures Department/Category change records. The MENU003 report should leverage the same underlying audit data to populate the new From/To columns.

Requested Timeline

Aligned with Priority: Medium

Preferred Quarter: Not specified

Target Version: Not specified

Notes: No hard deadline provided by requester.

Alternatives Considered

Not provided by requester. One alternative could be directing users to continue using the Audit Log for Department/Category change review, but this was rejected as it requires manual cross-referencing between two separate tools.

Original Description (preserved by INF Prod. Studio)

Background

Hotels may add or change menu items, and the related Department/Category configuration can impact inventory cost calculation results.

Currently, the Department/Category change record can be viewed in Audit Log, but MENU003 Item Maintenance Report does not clearly show this change information for maintenance review.

Requirement

Enhance MENU003 Item Maintenance Report to support displaying Department/Category change details.

Add a report parameter option, for example: Include changes for Department/Category.

Default value should be Off / No, to keep the current report behavior unchanged.

When the option is enabled, the report should include additional columns:

- Department/Category (From)

- Department/Category (To)

The report should show the changed value before and after the update, based on the existing item maintenance/audit log record logic.

Acceptance Criteria

- MENU003 report provides a new parameter to control whether Department/Category changes are included.

- The new parameter is disabled by default.

- When disabled, MENU003 keeps the current layout and output logic.

- When enabled, MENU003 displays Department/Category change columns in the report.

- The Department/Category From/To values should match the actual change record shown in Audit Log.

- The change should apply to both report preview and printed/exported report output, if applicable.
